browserCharts.title: Navigation completion
browserCharts.comment: Elapsed navigation time for the controlled incident page. Lower is better.

browserCharts.title: First contentful paint
browserCharts.comment: Time to the first contentful paint. Browser paint scheduling can produce quantized observations; lower is better.

browserCharts.title: Optimistic feedback
browserCharts.comment: Time from the claim event to visible optimistic feedback, before authoritative settlement. Lower is better.

browserCharts.title: Authoritative settlement
browserCharts.comment: Time from the claim event to the authoritative owner and version appearing in the DOM, including controlled-service work. Lower is better.

browserCharts.title: Warm browser used heap
browserCharts.comment: Post-GC browser used heap after the warm claim scenario. It includes V8 code and metadata; the separate composition chart uses an unprofiled snapshot capture.

sustained.title: Sustained Node throughput - c32
sustained.comment: Aggregate completed requests per second across 50 balanced 500 ms windows, including final drain. The mean and percentiles describe individual window rates; response validation runs outside each timed window. Higher is better.

burst.title: 16-request Node burst completion
burst.comment: Elapsed time for all 16 requests in each finite burst to complete, without replacement requests. Response validation follows the timer. Lower is better.

sequential.title: Warm sequential response latency
sequential.comment: Measured warm sequential response latency in this capture. Compare the full distribution alongside its arithmetic mean.

saturationCharts.title: Sustained Node throughput - c1
saturationCharts.comment: Aggregate completed requests per second across 50 balanced 500 ms windows, including final drain. The mean and percentiles describe individual window rates; response validation runs outside each timed window. Higher is better.

bars.title: SSR response size
bars.comment: Complete SSR document bytes for the same incident page. This includes framework resumption and controlled comparison data.

Aggregate RPS divides total completed requests by total actual window time including drain; percentiles and mean describe window rates.
Finite concurrency waves report burst completion time and are not sustained capacity measurements.
The load client retains response bodies for each window until deferred validation; local client, service, and server resource contention remains part of this setup.
Latency uses warm keep-alive requests over unthrottled local loopback.
Every SSR route loads the same fixture through the controlled service before rendering.
Saturation levels use sustained closed-loop local windows rather than an external open-loop load generator.
Render-only and equal-payload lanes are attribution diagnostics and do not replace end-to-end framework results.
Post-GC slopes are leak signals across a bounded run, not proof of unbounded retention.
Each participant declares its production transport per runtime; transport identity is recorded with every result.
